subject: LLM data use & transfers — DPA review and clarifications
messages:
From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@aureliahealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurelia Health Legal <legal@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on LLM data use & transfer — DPA review

Vanessa —

Thanks again for the quick turnaround on the DPA. I reviewed the redline and have a few open items we need clarified before our legal counsel will sign:

1) No‑training / model improvement: the current DPA language is a little fuzzy about whether customer prompts/responses may be used to improve models. We need an explicit "no model training or improvement" commitment unless we opt in.

2) Prompt/response ownership: our security folks want an unambiguous statement that all prompt content and generated responses remain customer property and are not used to claim downstream IP.

3) Subprocessors: the attached CSV shows some partner names but we need a guaranteed notification window and a subprocessor attestation for any changes.

4) Data transfers: can you confirm whether Redwood relies on SCCs for EU→US transfers or if there is any other transfer mechanism (e.g., EU region residency option)? We need to know whether our PHI adjacency restricts anything.

I've attached a marked DPA and our current subprocessor matrix. Can you loop in your privacy/legal and provide proposed language or evidence we can pass to our counsel?

Thanks —
Michael Torres
Sr. Counsel, Aurelia Health

- Laura, can you prepare the latest subprocessor attestation and the SCCs we hold?
- Michael, would you be available for a 30–45 minute call tomorrow to walk legal teams through the technical controls (log isolation, retention, and attestation)?

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Michael Torres <michael.torres@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on LLM data use & transfer — DPA review and clarifications

Michael / Vanessa —

Thanks — below are concrete options and proposed language you can drop into the redline. I kept the drafting concise so your counsel can review quickly.

1) No‑training (model improvement) option — proposed clause:
"Customer Data Exclusion for Model Improvement." "Redwood shall not use Customer Data (including prompts, messages, documents, or model outputs) to train, fine‑tune, or improve any machine learning models, unless Customer provides an explicit, written opt‑in for such uses. For clarity, Redwood may use aggregated telemetry that does not contain Customer Data for operational monitoring and service quality metrics."

2) Prompt/response ownership — proposed clause:
"Customer Content and Output Ownership." "Customer retains all rights, title, and interest in and to Customer Data and Customer Outputs. Redwood expressly disclaims any ownership or derived rights in Customer Data, prompts, and generated outputs and will not assert rights to use Customer Outputs for productization or model training absent an express license from Customer."

3) Subprocessors and notification: we can commit to 30 days prior notice for new subprocessors for core data processing, and provide an attestation package (contract excerpts, SOC/ISO cert references) upon request. For urgent operational patches we can offer a 10‑day expedited notice with a documented exception process.

4) Data transfers / SCCs / residency: Redwood supports SCCs and will execute SCCs as part of the DPA. We also offer regional isolation (EU region residency) for certain Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted customers can elect no‑train + data residency controls as an add‑on — we should confirm which deployment Aurelia intends to use.

I attached a one‑page redline excerpt for insertion (see attachment: redline_excerpt_no_training.docx) and a short matrix of controls. Happy to refine wording with their counsel.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Privacy & Legal Ops | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@aureliahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on LLM data use & transfer — DPA review and clarifications

Karthik —

Thanks for the language. A few follow‑ups from our side after circulating internally:

• Ownership/Outputs: we like the "Customer Outputs" wording but need assurance that any downstream derivatives created by Redwood teams (e.g., benchmark datasets, model variants) will not include Customer Outputs. Can you add an explicit line forbidding Redwood from using Customer Outputs to create derivative datasets or models?

• SCCs and evidence: please send the SCC templates you execute and a copy of the authority letter or the process for executing them. Also, can you confirm whether Redwood will sign the Aurelia‑modified SCCs or prefers to append your standard exhibit?

• Subprocessor attestations: the attestation package should include the date of the last audit and the scope (e.g., customer data processing permitted).

One practical question: if we take no‑training on the hosted Redwood product, will your observability (trace logs, token‑level cost telemetry) still be available to us? We need observability for debugging but don't want that data used for training.

On the call front — yes, we'd like a technical walkthrough with your security team.

—Michael

1) We will add a clear prohibition on Redwood creating derivative datasets or models that incorporate Customer Outputs; Karthik will add that sentence to the redline annex.
2) Laura will upload the SCC template and an attestation package (audit dates + scoping) to the Drive link and share with you by EOD PT. Link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Aurelia-DPA-Redline
